news.title: Amber Enterprises India Limited (NSEI:AMBER) completed the acquisition remaining 50% stake in Amber Resojet Private Limited from Lcgc Resolute Appliances Llp for INR 17.4 million.
news.body:
Amber Enterprises India Limited (NSEI:AMBER) agreed to acquire remaining 50% stake in Amber Resojet Private Limited from Lcgc Resolute Appliances Llp for INR 17.4 million on April 3, 2026. A cash consideration of INR 17.4 million will be paid by Amber Enterprises India Limited payable in one or more tranches. As part of consideration, INR 17.4 million is paid towards common equity of Amber Resojet Private Limited. Upon completion, Amber Enterprises India Limited will own 100% stake in Amber Resojet Private Limited.

No governmental or regulatory approvals are required. The acquisition is expected to be completed within 30 to 45 days from the execution date of the SPA.

news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings: Revenues exceed analysts expectations while EPS lags behind
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: ₹7.75 loss per share (down from ₹10.61 profit in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹29.4b (up 38% from 3Q 2025). Net loss: ₹272.4m (down 176% from profit in 3Q 2025). Revenue exceeded analyst estimates by 18%. Earnings per share (EPS) missed analyst estimates. Revenue is forecast to grow 18% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 15% growth forecast for the Consumer Durables industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 18% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 60% per year, which means it is tracking significantly ahead of earnings growth.

news.title: New major risk - Financial position
news.body: The company's debt is not well covered by operating cash flow. Operating cash flow to total debt ratio: 5.3% This is considered a major risk. If the company's operating cash flows are too small relative to the size of their debt, it increases their balance sheet risk. The company has less cash from operations to cover its expenses from servicing large debt and it increases the risk of liquidity issues. It also extends the time it would take for the company to pay back the debt in full, meaning it may not be able to easily pay it all off in a distress scenario. This is currently the only risk that has been identified for the company.
